title: Introspective quant-fidelity smoke suite and gate calibration for AWQ/GPTQ
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, fast-running smoke test suite and gate calibration process to detect regressions in output quality when deploying AWQ/GPTQ quantized variants (int8/int4) or changing quant profiles. The suite should run on model/config change events and produce an actionable signal with controlled false-positive rate for automated canary/rollback decisions.
background_and_rationale: We have observed intermittent quality regressions after deploying new quant profiles or changing AWQ/GPTQ parameters. Full eval harness runs are expensive and slow to iterate. This ticket creates an introspective smoke path that uses compact prompt cohorts, representative metrics, and statistically calibrated gates so that CI/canary automation can get fast coverage before promoting a build to production.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke-suite executes in <= 20 minutes on CI runners for a single model/profile
Per-model gate rules calibrated with explicit FPR/FNR targets (default: FPR <= 3%, FNR <= 10%)
Integration with rollout automation: a failing smoke check will block canary promotion and trigger the rollback playbook
Smoke run generates dashboard panel and artifact link in job output and GitHub PRs
Runbook documented and tested with one simulated regression scenario
metrics_and_signals: Delta-mean-logprob: average change in token log-prob across cohort
Semantic similarity: batch BERTScore and BARTScore deltas for generations
Task-specific metric: exact match / F1 for closed-response evals (QA/e2e templates)
Calibration signal: fraction of responses with > X divergence (configurable threshold)
Coverage: percentage of example set executed and model latency percentiles
sampling_strategy: Create 3 lightweight cohorts (sanity, edge-cases, high-impact prompts) sized 200/100/50 respectively
Prefer real production prompt samples when available; fall back to curated corpora per model family
Stratify by length and token distribution to capture KV-cache and sequence-length sensitivity
Rotate cohort members monthly and retain fixed seed for reproducibility
threshold_calibration_plan: Run baseline sweep across historical commits to estimate distribution of metric deltas
Fit per-model-profile Gaussian mixture or non-parametric quantiles to set gatepoints
Tune thresholds to target desired FPR/FNR tradeoff; record decision boundaries in config
Expose a ‘sensitivity’ knob for release engineers to relax/tighten gates during ramp
automation_and_integration: Hook smoke-suite into model-config-change webhook (model catalog + profile updates)
CI job artifact includes JSON summary, raw metric vectors, and link to failing examples
Rollout automation reads smoke result via API; failing results mark canary as unhealthy
Slack & email alerts for failing canary with triage checklist link
implementation_tasks: Define cohort sets and seed corpus for top 5 model families
Implement smoke harness as a lightweight runner that reuses existing eval code paths
Add telemetry and artifacts: per-example diffs, per-metric distributions
Create calibration job to compute thresholds from historical runs
Integrate with rollout service to read gate outputs and block promotions
Create dashboard panels and alerting rules in Grafana/Observability
open_decisions: Primary metric choice: aggregate logprob delta vs. BERTScore — currently leaning to combined signal
Cohort size tradeoff: smaller runs are faster but increase variance — default sizes above chosen by sampling experiments
Where to store calibration history: time series DB vs. long-term object store — prefer object store for reproducibility
risks_and_mitigations: False positives could slow releases — mitigation: conservative default thresholds and manual override
Overfitting thresholds to a small corpus — mitigation: rotate cohorts and validate on held-out weeks
Compute costs for frequent calibration jobs — mitigation: schedule nightly/weekly jobs depending on churn
